title: Market Pulse
body_html:
This post reflects my current views on the market, sectors, and internal breadth/momentum. Expect candid, data-driven analysis, peppered with personal insights drawn from years of trading experience. I aim to provide value in every edition, helping you to see the market through a clearer, more informed lens.

What You Can Expect

  • In-Depth Market Analysis: A thorough examination of market trends, key indices, and pivotal turning points.

  • Sector Spotlights: A closer look at the hottest (and not-so-hot) sectors, highlighting opportunities and risks.

  • Breadth and Momentum Insights: Understanding the underlying strength of the market through breadth indicators and momentum metrics.

  • Themes and Setups: A look at the top stocks in terms of relative strength, momentum, trend, volatility, and liquidity to spot themes, setups, and opportunities.

Exclusive Features

  • Interactive Spreadsheet: Alongside each post, I’ll link a detailed spreadsheet that tracks breadth and momentum metrics. This will allow you to follow along with the data and see the trends I’m analyzing day-by-day.

  • Quick Video Commentary: To complement the metrics, I’ll also be posting a quick video commentary several days a week. This will provide a more dynamic overview of the market, offering you additional context and clarity.

Market Metrics

Market Backdrop: Mixed

Major indices remain narrowly led. QQQ continues to hold up relatively better, but SPY has nearly undercut its breakout bar, adding pressure to an already fragile market. Mid- and small-cap indices weakened further, with MDY and IWM still below their 10-day, 20-day, and 50-day moving averages. The divergence remains clear: large caps are holding up better, but much of the broader market continues to struggle technically.

Sector leadership also remains narrow. Technology is still the clearest area of constructive action and has held its breakout levels. Healthcare is holding above recent pivot lows but has yet to generate meaningful upside follow-through. Energy ranks second in relative strength, but its technical structure remains weak. Most other sectors are still in poor or downtrending conditions, reinforcing the need to stay focused on true leadership rather than assume broad participation.

Breadth and momentum continue to carry a negative tilt. There has yet to be a meaningful expansion in new highs or in the number of stocks showing strong upside momentum. The next constructive step would be a clear increase in new highs and upside participation, which would help validate the large-cap breakouts and show that strength is beginning to broaden beneath the surface. Until that happens, there’s not much to do on the long side currently.

Tactical Plan of Action

1) Market Posture — Defensive to Selectively Constructive

QQQ is still holding up, but SPY is close to invalidating its breakout while MDY and IWM remain below their 10/20/50-day moving averages. Breadth is still weak, so the market has not earned broad aggression.

  • Keep exposure selective

  • Favor only the clearest leaders

  • Do not press until breadth improves and SPY stabilizes

2) Leadership

Primary focus: Technology
Secondary watch: Healthcare
Lower priority: Energy — strong RS, weak technical structure

Favor stocks near highs, above rising moving averages, and tightening around clean pivots. Avoid laggards, broken charts, and weak sectors.

3) Entries

Stay with the setups most consistent with historical winners:

  • VCPs and tight contractions

  • Clean breakout pivots

  • 2–5 day tight patterns / short flags

  • Controlled pullbacks to rising 10/20-day MAs

  • Catalyst-driven momentum setups with strong volume

Enter close to the pivot. Avoid chasing and avoid anticipatory entries in weak market conditions.

4) Position Size & Risk

Given the weak breadth and narrow leadership:

  • Risk roughly 0.20%–0.40% of account equity per trade

  • Start around ¼ to ½ normal size

  • Add only after the trade proves itself

  • Reserve larger size for A+ Technology leaders with immediate follow-through

  • Never average down

5) Trade Management

Momentum trades should work quickly.

  • Breakout falls back into base → reduce or exit

  • Loss of breakout-day low → reduce or exit

  • Loss of 10/20-day with weakening RS → reduce or exit

  • No progress after several sessions → reassess

  • Add only to winners; trail strong names with the 10-day or 20-day

6) What Changes the Posture

Press harder if:

  • SPY holds or reclaims its breakout

  • QQQ continues higher

  • New highs expand

  • Upside momentum overtakes downside momentum

  • MDY/IWM reclaim their 10/20-day MAs

Pull back further if:

  • SPY fully fails its breakout

  • QQQ loses its breakout structure

  • New lows expand

  • Technology leadership weakens

  • Breakout failures begin clustering

Bottom Line

The tape remains narrow, fragile, and selective. Technology is still providing opportunity, but weak breadth, poor mid/small-cap action, and pressure on SPY argue for restraint. The playbook is simple: trade only the strongest leaders, keep size small, demand confirmation, and cut failures fast.
